items.title: Specified small-perturbation material dynamics
items.statement:
Use the selected local material state, perfect stress branch, bulk-only relaxation branch, and unit conventions of [[post-tgr-perfect-fluid-model]], [[post-tgr-bulk-relaxation-model]], and [[def-tgr-framework-units]]. For this effective model take prescribed Minkowski spacetime $\mathbb R^4$ with coordinates $(x^0,\mathbf x)=(ct,\mathbf x)$, $t\in\mathbb R$, $\mathbf x\in\mathbb R^3$ measured in metres, and metric $\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$. The reference material is a constant state $(v_0,\sigma_{p0})$ in the supplier's open state domain, with supplied $e\in C^2$, $u_0=(1,0,0,0)$, $\Pi_0=0$, $n_0=1/v_0>0$, $\varepsilon_0=n_0e(v_0,\sigma_{p0})$, $p_0=-e_v(v_0,\sigma_{p0})$, $T_0=e_{\sigma_p}(v_0,\sigma_{p0})>0$, and enthalpy density $h_0=\varepsilon_0+p_0>0$. The local Gibbs supplier [[lem-tgr-local-gibbs-euler]] gives the dimensionless adiabatic response

$$a_s:=\left(\frac{\partial p}{\partial\varepsilon}\right)_{\sigma_p}=\frac{e_{vv}(v_0,\sigma_{p0})}{n_0h_0};$$

restrict this pair of effective branches to $a_s>0$. Here $e_{vv}$ is the second derivative of the supplied $C^2$ state function with respect to $v$ at fixed $\sigma_p$. The equality between the derivative and the state-function ratio is the exact interface stated by [[lem-tgr-local-gibbs-euler]] under the reference-state hypotheses above. The derivative is the local fixed-composition response at the reference state; the equation does not assign a universal value to $a_s$.

For this postulate, a first variation means the derivative at $\lambda=0$ of a smooth one-parameter family of field configurations through the reference state, with dimensionless $\lambda$; no member with $\lambda\ne0$ is required to solve a nonlinear equation. The fields $r,\widehat\Pi:\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R$ and $w:\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R^3$ are smooth. Write $r=\delta\varepsilon$, $w=(\delta u^1,\delta u^2,\delta u^3)$, and, in the bulk branch, $\widehat\Pi=\delta\Pi$. The adiabatic sector means $\delta\sigma_p=0$. These first variations have $r$ and $\widehat\Pi$ in Pa and $w$ and $a_s$ dimensionless. Let $\zeta_0>0$ and $\tau_0>0$ be the bulk viscosity and relaxation time evaluated at the reference state, with units Pa s and s. Spatial derivatives have units $\mathrm{m^{-1}}$ and $c$ has units $\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$.

Adopt the following two constant-coefficient effective systems on the stated background:

$$r_t+c h_0\operatorname{div}w=0,\qquad w_t+\frac{c a_s}{h_0}\nabla r=0$$

for the perfect branch, and

$$r_t+c h_0\operatorname{div}w=0,\qquad w_t+\frac{c}{h_0}\nabla(a_s r+\widehat\Pi)=0,\qquad \tau_0\widehat\Pi_t+\widehat\Pi=-\zeta_0c\operatorname{div}w$$

for the bulk-only branch. Derivatives $\nabla$ and $\operatorname{div}$ act on $\mathbf x$; $t$ is physical time and $c$ is the speed parameter in [[def-tgr-framework-units]]. The equations define the effective linear models. No uniform nonlinear error estimate, nonlinear solution lifespan, curved-spacetime evolution result, or existence claim for the nonlinear constitutive equations is postulated. The parameters and systems are adopted model inputs; they are not measurements or claims of universal material behavior.

For later solution claims, $\mathbb T_L^3:=(\mathbb R/L\mathbb Z)^3$ is the flat three-torus for $L>0$, and smooth periodic data mean $C^\infty$ maps on that quotient. A multi-index is a triple in $\mathbb N^3$. A Schwartz map $U_0:\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R^m$ means a $C^\infty$ map such that $x^\alpha\partial^\beta U_0(x)$ is bounded for every pair of multi-indices $\alpha,\beta$. The systems have $m=4$ and $m=5$ components, respectively.
items.physical_scope: Two stipulated adiabatic first-variation systems about a uniform Minkowski rest state, with positive response and bulk parameters; no nonlinear remainder or lifespan bound, curved-background evolution, empirical applicability, or measurement claim.

references.title: Éric Gourgoulhon, An Introduction to Relativistic Hydrodynamics, arXiv:gr-qc/0603009v1 (2006), §§4.2–4.3 and 5.1–5.4
references.locator: Full 37-page lecture-note PDF; PDF pp. 14–19: perfect stress, rest-frame energy and equation-of-state conventions, and local perfect-fluid balance projections.

references.title: Paul Romatschke, Relativistic Viscous Fluid Dynamics and Non-Equilibrium Entropy, arXiv:0906.4787v2 (2010), §§3.1 and 4.1
references.locator: Full 25-page paper; PDF pp. 7–11: small perturbations of a uniform state, bulk/shear relaxation parameters in high-frequency propagation, and non-equilibrium entropy-current context. Its vanishing-charge and higher-gradient model is not the exact branch adopted here.

references.title: Dirk H. Rischke, Microscopic Foundations of Relativistic Fluid Dynamics, lecture notes (May 2022), §§1.4.2–1.5 and 2.5.4
references.locator: Full 148-page lecture-note PDF; PDF pp. 20–27 and 52–53: transient bulk relaxation, quadratic entropy-current corrections, and model-specific stability/causality conditions. The source's fuller Israel–Stewart equations are not substituted for the stipulated effective system.

items.title: Causal stable perfect-material linear response
items.statement:
Assume the adiabatic perfect-material linear branch of [[post-tgr-linearized-material-model]] on its prescribed Minkowski background, with $c>0$, $h_0>0$, and $0<a_s\le1$, and assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. For every initial datum $U_0=(r_0,w_0)\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb R^4)$ or $U_0\in C^\infty(\mathbb T_L^3;\mathbb R^4)$ with $L>0$, the Cauchy problem $U(0,\cdot)=U_0$ for the system

$$r_t+c h_0\operatorname{div}w=0,\qquad w_t+\frac{c a_s}{h_0}\nabla r=0$$

has a unique global smooth solution on the corresponding space-time domain, contractive in the positive quadratic energy and its weighted Sobolev norms. Its energy density

$$\mathcal E_{\rm pf}=\frac12\left[\frac{a_s}{h_0}r^2+h_0|w|^2\right]$$

satisfies $\partial_t\mathcal E_{\rm pf}+\operatorname{div}(c a_s r w)=0$. For each Sobolev exponent $q\ge0$, its weighted Sobolev norm is nonincreasing for $t\ge0$. The characteristic speeds, meaning eigenvalues of the principal matrix in a unit spatial direction, are $0$ and $\pm c\sqrt{a_s}$. Finite propagation means that if initial data vanish on a ball of radius $R$, then at time $t$ they vanish on the concentric ball of radius $R-c\sqrt{a_s}\,t$ whenever $0\le t<R/(c\sqrt{a_s})$; on $\mathbb T_L^3$ use geodesic balls. Thus the exact linear propagation speed is $c\sqrt{a_s}\le c$. Equality is permitted at $a_s=1$. This is a conditional model deduction and makes no claim about nonlinear or curved-spacetime evolution, or about nature beyond the adopted model.
items.physical_scope: Adiabatic perfect-material first variations about the specified uniform Minkowski rest state with h0>0 and 0<a_s<=1; linear global evolution only, not nonlinear or curved-spacetime fluid existence or empirical applicability.

references.title: Éric Gourgoulhon, An Introduction to Relativistic Hydrodynamics, arXiv:gr-qc/0603009v1 (2006), §§4.2–4.3 and 5.1–5.4
references.locator: Full 37-page lecture-note PDF; PDF pp. 14–19: perfect-fluid stress and local balance projections. It does not establish a linear PDE existence theorem.

references.title: Paul Romatschke, Relativistic Viscous Fluid Dynamics and Non-Equilibrium Entropy, arXiv:0906.4787v2 (2010), §3.1
references.locator: Full 25-page paper; PDF p. 8: small perturbations around a uniform state and model-specific dispersion/propagation speeds, not finite-propagation existence for this branch.

references.title: Dirk H. Rischke, Microscopic Foundations of Relativistic Fluid Dynamics, lecture notes (May 2022), §2.5.4
references.locator: Full 148-page lecture-note PDF; PDF pp. 52–53: model-specific causality and stability analysis for transient fluid equations; the local theorem supplies the exact perfect branch used here.

items.title: Causal stable bulk-relaxation linear response
items.statement:
Assume the adiabatic bulk-only linear branch of [[post-tgr-linearized-material-model]] on its prescribed Minkowski background, with $h_0,T_0,c,a_s,\zeta_0,\tau_0>0$, the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, and

$$a_s+\frac{\zeta_0}{\tau_0h_0}\le1.$$

For every initial datum $U_0=(r_0,w_0,\widehat\Pi_0)\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb R^5)$ or $U_0\in C^\infty(\mathbb T_L^3;\mathbb R^5)$ with $L>0$, the Cauchy problem $U(0,\cdot)=U_0$ for the system

$$r_t+c h_0\operatorname{div}w=0,\qquad w_t+\frac{c}{h_0}\nabla(a_s r+\widehat\Pi)=0,\qquad \tau_0\widehat\Pi_t+\widehat\Pi=-\zeta_0c\operatorname{div}w$$

has a unique global smooth solution on the corresponding space-time domain and is contractive in its positive quadratic energy and weighted Sobolev norms. Its energy density

$$\mathcal E_{\rm bulk}=\frac12\left[\frac{a_s}{h_0}r^2+h_0|w|^2+\frac{\tau_0}{\zeta_0}\widehat\Pi^2\right]$$

satisfies $\partial_t\mathcal E_{\rm bulk}+\operatorname{div}[c(a_s r+\widehat\Pi)w]=-\widehat\Pi^2/\zeta_0$. For each Sobolev exponent $q\ge0$, its weighted Sobolev norm is nonincreasing for $t\ge0$. The characteristic speeds, meaning eigenvalues of the principal matrix in a unit spatial direction, are $0$ and $\pm c\sqrt{a_s+\zeta_0/(\tau_0h_0)}$. Finite propagation means that if initial data vanish on a ball of radius $R$, then at time $t$ they vanish on the concentric ball of radius $R-v_{\rm bulk}t$ whenever $0\le t<R/v_{\rm bulk}$, where $v_{\rm bulk}=c\sqrt{a_s+\zeta_0/(\tau_0h_0)}$; on $\mathbb T_L^3$ use geodesic balls. Hence propagation is bounded by $c$ under the stated inequality. Equality at the causal threshold is allowed. Energy contraction does not assert decay of every mode. The result is conditional on the adopted linear model; it is not a nonlinear or curved-spacetime existence claim or an empirical conclusion.
items.physical_scope: Adiabatic bulk-only first variations about the specified uniform Minkowski rest state with h0,T0,a_s,zeta,tau positive and a_s+zeta/(tau h0)<=1; linear evolution only, not nonlinear or curved-spacetime existence or empirical applicability.

references.title: Éric Gourgoulhon, An Introduction to Relativistic Hydrodynamics, arXiv:gr-qc/0603009v1 (2006), §§4.2–4.3 and 5.1–5.4
references.locator: Full 37-page lecture-note PDF; PDF pp. 14–19: perfect-fluid state and balance conventions. The bulk relaxation system is an additional restricted constitutive model.

references.title: Paul Romatschke, Relativistic Viscous Fluid Dynamics and Non-Equilibrium Entropy, arXiv:0906.4787v2 (2010), §§3.1 and 4.1
references.locator: Full 25-page paper; PDF pp. 8–11: second-order bulk transport parameters, high-frequency characteristic-speed conditions, and non-equilibrium entropy-current context. Its shear and zero-charge assumptions are not imported.

references.title: Dirk H. Rischke, Microscopic Foundations of Relativistic Fluid Dynamics, lecture notes (May 2022), §§1.4.2–1.5 and 2.5.4
references.locator: Full 148-page lecture-note PDF; PDF pp. 20–27 and 52–53: bulk relaxation and entropy-current structure, plus model-specific causality and stability analysis. The exact variable-coefficient law here is separately stipulated and its linear evolution is established by the mathematical supplier.

items.title: Perfect sound and neutral perturbation modes
items.statement:
Under $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, use the perfect linear branch of [[pthm-tgr-perfect-causal-linear-response]] with $h_0>0$, $0<a_s\le1$, and reference speed $c>0$. For any nonzero wave vector $\mathbf k\in\mathbb R^3$ in $\mathrm{m}^{-1}$ and real amplitude $A$ in Pa, define the dimensionless phase $\phi(t,\mathbf x)=\mathbf k\cdot\mathbf x-\omega t$, where $\omega=c\sqrt{a_s}\,|\mathbf k|$ has units $\mathrm{s}^{-1}$, and set

$$r(t,\mathbf x)=A\cos\phi(t,\mathbf x),\qquad w(t,\mathbf x)=\frac{A\omega}{c h_0|\mathbf k|^2}\,\mathbf k\cos\phi(t,\mathbf x).$$

This is an exact sound mode of the adopted linear system. At zero wave vector, the separate constant fields $r=r_0$ and $w=w_0$ are also exact solutions for arbitrary constants $r_0\in\mathbb R$ in Pa and $w_0\in\mathbb R^3$ dimensionless. Every nonzero such choice is a neutral mode, so linear energy contraction does not mean that every perturbation decays. These are calculated model solutions, not observations.
items.physical_scope: Explicit plane-wave and spatially constant solutions of the specified adiabatic perfect-material linear system; no claim that every mode decays, no nonlinear solution, and no empirical data.
